rationale:
lazygit is a single-binary Go CLI/TUI, so this follows the standard Go-from-tarball PKGBUILD pattern with a few package-specific adjustments.

- Source is the upstream GitHub release tarball for tag v0.64.1, matching the request URL. `pkgver` comes straight from the tag.
- The tree ships a committed `vendor/` directory with `vendor/modules.txt`, so `GOFLAGS` uses `-mod=vendor` (per the Go reference's vendoring note) instead of `-mod=readonly`, and no network module download happens during build or check.
- `build()` builds the single `main.go` binary directly with `go build -o lazygit .` rather than the `./cmd/...` multi-binary pattern, since lazygit only produces one binary.
- Standard hardening flags (`-buildmode=pie -trimpath`) and the external linker (`-linkmode=external`, for a build-id) are set, following the ecosystem reference. CGO_* flags are exported for completeness even though the project builds with CGO disabled upstream in its own release process; leaving CGO enabled here is harmless since the source has no cgo files, and it keeps CFLAGS/LDFLAGS hardening consistent if that ever changes.
- `-ldflags` also injects `-X main.version=$pkgver -X main.buildSource=archlinux`, mirroring the `main.go` build-time variables (`version`, `commit`, `date`, `buildSource`) so `lazygit --version` reports a real version instead of "unknown". `commit`/`date` are left unset since the release tarball carries no git metadata to source them from truthfully.

### Maintainer hint: failing integration/components test

- Investigated the failure: `pkg/integration/components/test_test.go` (a meta test of the test framework itself, not gated behind `-short`) calls `lazycoreUtils.GetLazyRootDirectory()`, which is defined in `vendor/github.com/jesseduffield/lazycore/pkg/utils/utils.go`. That function walks up from the working directory looking for a `.git` entry and calls `log.Fatal("must run in lazy project folder or child folder")` if it reaches `/` without finding one.
- A GitHub release/tag tarball (unlike a git checkout) contains no `.git` directory, so this always fails when building from the tarball source the pipeline uses.
- Confirmed via `runner.go`'s `createFixture` that the returned root path is only ever used to build paths into files that genuinely ship in the tarball (e.g. `test/global_git_config`) — nothing downstream requires an actual git repository or its metadata.
- Fix: in `check()`, create an empty placeholder `.git` directory before running `go test ./... -short`, then remove it afterward. This satisfies `os.Stat(path/.git)` on the very first loop iteration (the project root), which is exactly correct since that iteration starts at the module root where `go test` runs, so no fake metadata or wrong-directory risk is introduced. This keeps the upstream test suite intact and passing without patching vendored code or skipping the package.

dependencies.reasoning: lazygit is a statically-oriented Go binary with no runtime library dependencies beyond glibc (the binary is dynamically linked via -linkmode=external). It shells out to the user's own `git` at runtime but that's a well-known, near-universal system tool that Arch's packaging norms treat as an assumed/optional runtime dependency rather than a hard `depends` entry for this kind of tool, similar to how other git-wrapping CLIs are packaged; users of a git TUI overwhelmingly already have git installed. `go` is required only to compile the vendored module tree; no other makedepends are needed since vendor/ makes the build fully offline and base-devel already covers general build tooling.

license.reasoning: LICENSE at the source root is the standard MIT license text (Copyright (c) 2018 Jesse Duffield), matching the requested license and upstream's own declaration. MIT is a well-known SPDX identifier so only the license file needs installing to /usr/share/licenses/lazygit, no LicenseRef needed.

deviations: Added a `.git` placeholder directory creation/removal in check() that isn't part of the standard Go PKGBUILD reference template, to work around the upstream test suite's project-root detection failing on a git-metadata-free release tarball (see rationale and maintainer hint above). No other deviations from the Go ecosystem reference.
